name: Scythe (horizontal undercutter bar spinner)
size_rule: robot/profile.py aws2025: 150 mm floor square, no overhang at any height, no height limit. All values are derived by the src/scythe/params.py relations (the bar is energy- and pitch-limited: the cantilevered undercutter keeps its stored energy under the 20 J spinner escalation threshold and its tip clears the floor at the 5 deg hop pitch), POD_W 65, vertical-wall rear pod, wheels behind the sweep.

weapon_lock.note: made safe outside the robot: the XT30 is unplugged and a 3 mm pit pin dropped through the panel, floor and bar lock holes rests on the floor slab, so the bar cannot turn past it; the pin is a pit tool, not part of the build

parts.sharp_corners_ok: the flagged concave corners are where the vertical-wall pod meets the sloped disc and the roots of the cradle ribs and panel posts on the shell: short compression ribs and a bonded seam, the same class as the hspin_bar chassis halves
parts.label: printed PA tub: sloped disc over the bar + vertical-wall rear pod, motor housing tube, weapon boss, N10 cradles, panel posts

parts.sharp_corners_ok: the concave corners are the disc/pod seam of the top outline, carried on the printed wall below: a skin seam, not a load-bearing notch
parts.label: 1 mm PA-CF top skin: the tension skin the weapon boss hangs from; M2 button screws into printed posts
bl_1806 fixed half, flange up: 4x M2 down through the panel and boss into the flange taps
bl_1806 bell: cap down on the hub, spins with the bar; the motor's own shaft (wshaft) is a press fit in its bored core
3 mm Hardox two-tooth bar, energy/pitch-limited length, horizontal under the tub; csk M2.5s, piloted on the motor's own shaft
turned 7075 hub on the motor's own shaft: its cup pilots on the bell cap rim, the bar bolts to it with 2x M2.5

parts.stock: 3 mm silver steel rod, M3 thread 8 at the lower end
parts.label: the motor's own shaft, extended: press fit in the bell's bored core, down through hub and bar to the M3 nut thread
M3 nut on the shaft's lower thread: clamps bar + hub up against the bell cap face

parts.exposed_reason: the N10's shaft and the wheel it drives are outside the pod wall by design, exactly like Revron's outboard belt drives; the gearbox body is inside
parts.label: right drive: body nested against the pod wall, clamped between gearbox face and wheel

parts.exposed_reason: the N10's shaft and the wheel it drives are outside the pod wall by design, exactly like Revron's outboard belt drives; the gearbox body is inside
parts.label: left drive: mirror of the right
2S 300 mAh HV pack in the pod behind the motors; a poly strap through printed slots holds it down (the strap carries the inverted load)
20 A brushless ESC on the pod floor ahead of the motors, bonded on a foam pad
Malenki-Nano combined drive ESC + receiver, taped to the top panel's underside ahead of the weapon housing
mini switch in its bay at the pod's rear, clamped to the top panel by its own bushing and nut through the 4 mm key hole

connections.reason: the bar's 3.1 mm bore pilots on the motor's own shaft (0.05 mm slide): the shaft centres the bar, the clamp nut sets its height and the M2.5s carry the torque
the hub's 3.2 mm bore runs on the shaft (0.1 mm slide): the shaft locates it, the clamp and the bar screws carry the torque
the motor's own shaft, a press fit in the bell's bored rotor core (the catalogue draws the bore at r1.45); the nut clamps bar + hub to the bell cap face so the stack turns as one
the hub's top cup pilots on the bell's cap rim and the clamp nut seats it hard on the cap face: torque passes through the clamped faces and the shaft's press fit
M3 thread on the shaft's lower end: the thread is the key, and the nut clamps bar + hub up against the bell cap face
2x M2.5 csk through the bar into the hub's tapped holes
4x M2 through the panel and the printed boss into the stator flange taps: the boss ties the stator to the tension skin
8x M2 button through the panel into the printed posts (thread-forming, Revron top-panel style)
wheel D-bore on the 3 mm D-shaft: the flat carries the drive torque; the wheel boss clamps the pod wall between gearbox and wheel so the motor cannot walk inboard
wheel D-bore on the 3 mm D-shaft: the flat carries the drive torque; the wheel boss clamps the pod wall between gearbox and wheel so the motor cannot walk inboard
gearmotor seats on its printed cradle pads, the ribs locate it fore-aft and the pod wall takes the gearbox face; the wheel on the shaft clamps the assembly
gearmotor seats on its printed cradle pads, the ribs locate it fore-aft and the pod wall takes the gearbox face; the wheel on the shaft clamps the assembly
the pack sits on a velcro pad on the pod floor and a poly strap through printed slots holds it down: the strap carries the inverted load, the pad only locates
the switch's mounting bushing passes through the panel's 4 mm key hole and its nut clamps it: the key hole is the interlock

allow_overlap.reason: the motor's own shaft is a press fit in the bell's bored core (the catalogue draws the bore at r1.45, the shaft is r1.5)
the wheel's D-bore is cut 0.1 mm large on the flat sides so it slides on; the D-flat keys the drive
